title: TS-58 Reconcile a computer record left stale by a killed host
description: From the TS-56 live rehearsal: after the TS-53 cleanup killed the host with ecs stop-task before it could report, the computer record still said stopped=false and disk_dirty=true with no running task and the dirty data gone, and it stayed that way into the next rehearsal. A crash, spot reclaim or manual stop would do the same in production. Decide and implement the reconciliation: the starter or the next start (conversation/src/domain/computers.ts, computer-start.ts, host-starter.ts; the host's lease and heartbeat timeout in domain/workers.ts) must detect that the recorded host is gone (no heartbeat within the timeout, ECS task not running) and settle the record: stopped=true, release the live-writer lock, and decide what disk_dirty means when the live disk is lost (the unpublished writes are lost: the snapshot generation stays the last published one; record that the disk must hydrate from the snapshot, hydrate_required=true) so a recycle never serves a record that claims a running host or a dirty disk that no longer exists. Cucumber scenarios (host killed mid-turn, then a new turn) with mutation checks, and a live re-run of the TS-53 flow with a manual ecs stop-task to prove it.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Merged via PR 462. settleComputerIfHostLost in requestComputerHostStart; design in docs 4.3.1. Live re-check pending: kill a host with ecs stop-task mid-turn, then a new turn must settle the record (hydrate_required with a snapshot) and complete.

comments.author: home
comments.text: LIVE PROOF, development, PASS. Run 1: write_workspace then ecs stop-task 0.6 s after the tool.result (crash simulation): record stale as predicted (stopped=false, disk_dirty=true, 0 tasks). Run 2: a new turn settled the record on the first poll (stopped=true, disk_dirty=false, hydrate_required=true), a new host hydrated, ts56.txt read back ts56-hello-snapshot and the dead host's unpublished file was missing (as designed), turn.completed in 34 s; stored item has host_lost_at and host_lost_generation=4 (the killed generation). Cleanup: 0 tasks, DLQs 0. Not shown on GET /orgs/{t}/computer (see TS-55). Nothing reaps the stale record before the next start (by design).

right_now_summary: A live test confirmed the next turn repairs the stale record and restores the disk from its last snapshot.
